# 18-careforce — sources

Back-test entry `18-careforce.yaml`: Careforce, AI agents that call and book the patients a health center never reaches
(YC Fall 2024). Written 2026-10-22 from public material only, read that day. Quotes are verbatim from the page named.
"Author's choice" marks the smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent. The launch era is the
Launch YC post of 2024-11-22 and the weeks around it (the founder's gap-11 rule: every figure pinned to the launch era
where one exists; anything later is marked as later, and a later price sits under *Status today*).

Main sources (short names used below):
- [LYC] Launch YC: "Careforce - Must-have AI agents for Healthcare admin", 2024-11-22 (created_at in the page data) — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/MJj-careforce-must-have-ai-agents-for-healthcare-admin

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Medical assistants at community health centers, who work the outreach lists between patients.
   [LYC] "For health centers & practices this means MAs (short-staffed with front desk and intake) end up spending most
   of their time on admin tasks and most patients are never outreached & scheduled for vital screenings/visits,
   leaving a 1/3rd of care unserviced." → `roles[assistant]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: of
   [LYC]'s three segments (health centers and practices; digital health and CCM companies; payers) the first, the one
   the post describes by its staff.

2. **What (the job).** Get every patient due for a screening or visit called and booked.
   [LYC] "Most care coordination & data sharing is still manually done by staff through phones, email, fax because of
   unintegrated systems and custom workflows too unique to automate out of the box." → `statements.problem`,
   `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** Each working day, when the list of due patients has to be called between patients.
   [LYC] "Outreach using 50+ editable scripts (mammograms, pre-post-op, onboarding etc.)"; "Leave Voicemails, Sending
   reminders, and autonomously retry patients as needed". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: outreach call list`.
   Author's choice: the window {5, WORKING_DAYS} (spec 120: a daily rhythm in a clinic read as working days) and
   Frequency 3 to 5 working days out of 5; [LYC] gives no count. Prevalence `p_80_100` follows from "most patients are
   never outreached".

4. **Which people.** US community health centers (FQHCs) and primary-care practices that work outreach lists by phone.
   [LYC] "Our AI agents are already Live with health centers and digital health companies helping analyze, call,
   schedule, and generate revenue." → `context.segment`, `market: US` (a San Francisco company, [KFF]).

5. **Who pays.** The health center. [LYC] "Let us take on your calling, coordination, and manual admin work so you can
   get more patients in the door without burning out your staff."; "increase revenue with Careforce AI Agents".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: director}`. Author's choice: the decider is the health center's executive or
   operations director and the tested role "The CFO" (a second role, "The board", listed: FQHCs are governed by
   boards). Purchase friction's three items (a HIPAA security review — tested; giving the agent access to the EMR; a
   board vote) are the author's, from [LYC]'s "Use EMR, Scheduling, payer and provider portals through UI or API
   Integrations" and [KFF]'s note that plans "are responsible for ensuring that technology complies with state and
   federal regulations, including patient privacy and data security". Commitment's step, "try it on one outreach list":
   [LYC] "We'd love to learn about your use cases and give you personalized demos unique to your use case."; the
   wording is the author's.

6. **Mechanism.** Two agents: one calls, texts, emails and books; one pulls data and builds the lists.
   [LYC] "Careforce creates autonomous agents that are able to take on these human-glue tasks and complete them in the
   same way as your staff would without the need for integrations." [LYC] (Angelica) "Call, text, email, and schedule
   patients autonomously"; "Speak in 29 Languages to engage and educate across demographics"; "Make 100 calls / min.
   and finish a year's worth of outreach in weeks". [LYC] (David) "Prepare reports, and generate lists for Angelica to
   realize the unrealized revenue". → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`; Compatibility (the list straight out
   of the EMR — tested; open slots; patients picking up unknown numbers) and Adoption friction (hand the day's list to
   an AI caller — tested; take the calls it hands back, from [KFF] "This will always be, in my opinion, an AI-human
   combination"). Relative advantage's two benefits are [LYC]'s retries (fewer_attempts) and "finish a year's worth
   of outreach in weeks" (shorter_time); the wording is the author's.

7. **Price and cost.** No price is public at launch or today: [LYC] offers demos, [WB] has no pricing page near launch,
   [SITE] has none today. The founder's price, AMOUNT_PERIOD **$1,500 to $3,000 per health center a month**, is the
   operator's reading: a monthly per-site fee of the size community health centers pay for a part-time outreach caller's
   share of work (an MA's hour is about $22, [BLS]; $1,500 to $3,000 is roughly 70 to 135 such hours), set below what
   the bookings it claims to recover would bring in. It is said in `statements.commercial` as the founder would type
   it, and marked there and in the header as the operator's.
   Existing sacrifice, RATE about **30% to 33%** of the patients due for a visit or screening per health center a month,
   lost as "Visits and screenings never booked because nobody reached the patient": [LYC]'s "1/3rd of care unserviced"
   for health centers (33%) and "costing 30% in bookings" across healthcare (30%). Ability to pay is read `budget` by
   the engine (a percent of patients never compares with an amount a month), so the directors answer the budget item.

8. **Occasions.** The stories are scripted from [LYC]'s scripts list (mammograms, pre-post-op), the short-staffing it
   names, and [KFF]; no respondent is a real person. [KFF] (Kern's CEO) "But we are already stretched thin. We need this
   functionality to be much more effective and augment our efforts." [KFF] "In samples of actual conversations provided
   to a reporter, Angelica sounded lifelike at first, although more than once cross-talk with a patient caused the
   program to pause suddenly."

The split on Price (4 of the 7 who name a rung at $1,500 or above) is the author's: no public account gives what a
health center would pay. No respondent carries the name of a customer, patient, official or founder in the sources.

## Status today

Same idea, traction moved to health plans. [SITE] still sells the two agents for payors, plans, FQHCs and specialties.
The public customers are Medi-Cal health plans doing renewal outreach: [KFF] "Kern Family has spent about $370,000 on the
software by Careforce, a San Francisco startup, to facilitate rapid and repeated outreach to members when it's time to
renew their coverage."; "estimated it would have had to spend $2.4 million in staffing costs to match the program's more
than 800,000 calls to its 387,000 members"; "Kern Family's Medi-Cal renewal rate in April was 94.9%". [CHCF] "With the
aid of Careforce, KFHC renewed 96% of their members during the first year, compared to 38% before using the AI platform."
[KFF] says the agent "speaks more than 30 languages" (29 at launch). Price today: not public.

## Could not be sourced

- **A price, at any time.** The founder's $1,500 to $3,000 per health center a month is the operator's reading (item 7);
  the only public money figure is one health plan's cumulative spend ([KFF], 2026), not a unit price.
- **A health center's share of patients never booked, measured.** The 30% to 33% are the founders' own launch claims
  (one for health centers, one for healthcare overall), not a study.
- **A buyer title.** [LYC] asks "Healthcare Orgs" for demos; the director as decider, the CFO and the board as the roles,
  and the three Purchase friction items are the author's.
- **First-person MA accounts.** None public; the occasions are scripted from [LYC] and [KFF] (a health plan, not a
  health center).
- **A launch-era site.** [WB] holds no snapshot between 2024-05-18 and 2025-11-13; the launch post is the only
  launch-era page. [CHCF] could not be fetched directly (a bot check); its quote is as the diversity research read it.
- An MA's hour: [BLS]'s median stands in; no cost in the entry is in hours.

founder.order_why: It runs from naming and market to the context, its time window, then belief about the problem, the current way and who asks. Each step builds on the one before, so nothing feels out of place.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies'), with the window screen between them; if 5 is only a review of 3 it should say so.
founder.missing: What the unreached patients cost the health center (my launch claim is a third of care unserviced, about 30% of bookings lost), and the fact that the medical assistant feels the problem but the director pays. Nothing asks about the two-agent solution, the price per health center a month, or the director as the buyer.

PRIMARY.order_why: The yes/no and the how-many-days questions make sense first, but asking what I'd most like made easier before asking about my last outreach call feels backwards, since thinking about the actual call first would help me pick.
PRIMARY.asked_twice: Screens 1 and 2 overlap: 'did you get every one of them booked' in the last 5 days and 'on how many days did you get every one booked' are basically the same question, and the second already answers the first.
PRIMARY.missing: How many patients were on my list each day; what kept me from finishing, like getting pulled to room patients or cover front desk and intake; patients not answering, wrong numbers or full voicemails; needing an interpreter or calling in Spanish; and whether the patients I reached actually agreed to book, for example for a mammogram.

screens.why4: Two distinct voices, each with a preview, Daphne preselected, and switching is free; nothing is missing, because a text-only route is already covered by people being able to read and tap.
screens.why5: Nothing of my study is changed here, and no mention of Careforce, Angelica or the director roles reaches the respondent through the interviewer.

screens.why1: Right after choosing who asks the questions, it makes sense to choose how my medical assistants will answer before the study goes out.
screens.why2: I sell AI agents that call patients, so an AI interviewer is plain to me, but "Still recording" under Daphne makes me read twice to work out whether it means her voice is still being made or something is recording now.
screens.why3: I know my MAs answer between patients, often at a loud front desk, so I can judge whether they would rather tap through text or talk to Daphne.
screens.why4: Text, AI voice and letting them pick cover the real choices, each is distinct, and each says when it is ready.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles is shown, and my pick, Read and tap, is kept as I made it.
screens.instead: How should medical assistants answer? — AI interviewer · Daphne (her voice is being prepared, ready in a few minutes) / Read and tap (ready now) / Let them choose (ready when Daphne is)

screens.why1: After choosing how medical assistants answer, the last step is to say who receives the link, so the question is obviously in place.
screens.why2: 'By name' and 'one open link' are plain to me, but 'a search on the Contacts page' points to a Keel page I have not seen in this flow, so I had to read that option twice.
screens.why3: I know whether I am sending to MAs I know at the health centers we are live with or posting in an MA group, so I can answer this from my own work.
screens.why4: Named people, a Keel-found list and an open group link are the three real ways I would reach medical assistants, and they are distinct; no escape is needed because one of them always fits.
screens.why5: My pick, each MA by name, is kept, and nothing of Careforce, Angelica or the director roles appears.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? — People I know by name (I send each one their own link) / People Keel finds for me (Keel searches for medical assistants; I pick from the list and send each a link) / A group, with one open link (I post it where medical assistants already are; each signs in with Google)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title with 'Frequency: 4 answered' beside it, but the deciding gap (4 of the 5 needed) only appears down on the card, and nothing says why 4 of the 7 who answered count for Frequency, Importance and Current solution.
screens.why_b2: The stage page has no chart; the tally (1 holding, 3 too few, 7 answered) and Prevalence's '6 of 7 · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar' are plain, but I have to look twice to see why 7 answered yet only 4 are counted on three cards.
screens.why_b3: Importance and Current solution are word for word what I checked, but Prevalence and Frequency read 'got every one of them booked', with no 'them' to point to, and sound like my MAs succeed, which is the opposite of my problem.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' hints that I need one more answer on three beliefs, but no line tells me what this means for Careforce or what to do next.
screens.why_b5: The numbers stay visible and 'at the bar' is honest, but 'Holding up' beside 'got every one of them booked' reads as if MAs book every due patient, which overstates something my people never claimed.
screens.instead: Too few to call yet: only 4 of the 7 MAs who answered could be counted on Frequency, Importance and Current solution, and each needs 5; get at least one more MA who works an outreach list. Prevalence held at the bar: 6 of 7 had patients due for a call in the last 5 working days.

screens.why_b1: 'Holding up' sits beside '6 of 7 said yes, bar 6 of 7', but the belief says my MAs got every patient booked, so a held verdict reads as my problem not existing and I can't tell which way it cuts.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 7 cells, 6 for me and 1 against, on an axis from 0 to 7, with the marker at 6, so what is counted, over how many and where the bar sits are plain at once.
screens.why_b3: I never claimed 8 in 10 MAs got every one booked; my belief is that most of the day's list is left uncalled, and this line states the opposite of what I typed.
screens.why_b4: The So line only points to the next two cards and says nothing about what a common occasion means for Angelica taking the outreach list.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said ('a small group: a lean, not a call'), but counting 'got every one booked' answers for me treats MAs who finished their list as evidence of the problem, which the answers cannot carry.
screens.instead: At least 8 in 10 MAs had a list of due patients still to call in the last 5 working days: 6 of 7 did, right at your bar; a lean from 7, not a call.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside '5 needed to call it', but the line under it says '4 answered' while the count line says '6 answered · 4 counted', so I have to work out that the deciding number is four counted, not four answered.
screens.why_b2: The axis (working days out of 5), the median at 4 and the four people are plain, but 'your bar · 3 of 4' reads at first as if 3 of 4 met it, when it actually means 3 of 4 are needed and all 4 are inside.
screens.why_b3: I recognise my 3-to-5-days belief, but 'every one of them booked' leaves 'them' hanging; it should name the patients due for a screening or visit, the way my circumstance does.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that one more clear answer would settle it, or that all four counted so far lean my way.
screens.why_b5: The screen says the group is small ('a lean, not a call'), names the two who weren't counted and why, and does not call the belief held even though all four counted answers fall inside.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of the 6 who answered could be counted (Marisol would rather not say, Darnell guessed), and 5 are needed; all 4 booked every due patient on 3 or more days, so one more clear answer would settle it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats the same 4 and 5.
screens.why_b2: The caption says plainly that 4 people each picked two and the bars count 8 picks, but the strip that should show one cell per person has 8 cells (3 for, 5 against), so I had to work out that Olga is the only person actually against me.
screens.why_b3: The title Importance and the belief line are word for word what I checked on the way in, with my 'Reaching patients due for a screening' marked as the problem I named.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that one more counted MA settles it, or that 3 of 4 already sits above my 2-in-3 bar.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said and no call is made, but tagging every other pick 'against' (5 against vs 3 for) makes it look like the room went against me, when 3 of the 4 people put it in their two.
screens.instead: 3 of the 4 counted put reaching patients in their two (Olga, who has an outreach coordinator, didn't), already above your 2-in-3 bar; one more counted medical assistant will call it, so send the study to a few more.

screens.why_b1: The status "Too few to call" sits right beside the deciding number, "5 needed to call it", so I know at once that nothing is decided and why.
screens.why_b2: The rungs, the 'below here' line and the per-rung for/against counts are plain, but "your bar · 3 of 4" reads as if my bar were 3 of 4 when 3 of 4 is the result against a 2-in-3 bar, and the ghost fifth cell needs a second look to see it is the missing answer.
screens.why_b3: The title is Current solution and the belief line is word for word the one I checked about calling, texting and faxing falling short.
screens.why_b4: "Nothing is settled here yet" is generic; it doesn't tell me that 3 of my 4 counted MAs fell short, or that one more counted answer from an MA working a list would settle it.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said ("a lean, not a call"), but the headline's "4 answered" contradicts the count line's "6 answered · 4 counted", which makes it look like two of my MAs never replied.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted fell short of 'most called' (6 answered, 2 not counted); one more counted answer decides it, so send the study to another MA who works an outreach list.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no answer yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: The Importance name and the belief line are word for word the ones I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: The screen implies I need at least one more answer, but it never says so outright, and it says nothing about what Olga's coordinator escape means for who I sell to.
screens.why_b5: The single quote is counted as one against out of one asked, and the status keeps n=4 in view, so nothing is stretched past the people who answered.
screens.why_b6: Olga shows me something I did not type: where a dedicated outreach coordinator works the list, the MA's real pain is prior auths and rooming on a packed schedule, which hints that my buyer is the clinic without a coordinator.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 answered, so get one more medical assistant to answer. The one who did not pick outreach has a coordinator who clears the list every day, so check whether your clinics have one.

screens.why1: As the first screen it should check whether I worked a due list this week, but it asks whether I booked every patient, and since a gate 'No' ends the interview, nearly every MA I know gets cut, even though we all called a list.
screens.why2: 'Every one of them' has nothing before it to point to, so on first hearing I don't know who 'them' is: my patients, the due list, the mammogram callbacks?
screens.why3: If I knew it meant my outreach list, I'd know straight off whether I got through and booked all of them; I didn't, I never do when we're short at the front desk.
screens.why4: Yes and No are fine, but a gate takes no escape and this one shows two, 'I'd rather not say' isn't allowed, and 'I can't recall one particular outreach call' doesn't answer a question about booking everyone.
screens.why5: The founder's job is getting every due patient called and booked, but the screen turns that goal into a pass-or-fail test of whether I finished, which drifts from asking whether I do this work at all.
screens.why6: It's short and ends 'Yes or no', but heard aloud with no list named first, 'them' leaves me asking 'who?' before I can answer.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you call patients from a list of those due for a screening or visit? Yes or no.

screens.why1: It follows the yes-or-no about the week, but the screen before already asked whether I got every one of them booked, so asking it again day by day feels like the same question twice.
screens.why2: "Every one of them" points back to a list this screen never names, so I'd have to remember it means the day's call list of patients due for a screening or visit.
screens.why3: I work the list between rooming patients, and half of them don't pick up or need a callback, so whether a day was all booked is something I'd have to guess at.
screens.why4: The true answer for most of my weeks is none, not one day where every patient on the list got booked, and there's no 0 or "none of the days" to pick.
screens.why5: It's about calling and booking patients due for screenings, which is my job, and nothing about anybody's product shows.
screens.why6: Short, one question, and "a number from 1 to 5" is easy to hold when heard, with the escape said last.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, on how many days did you get everyone on that day's call list booked? None; 1 or 2 days; 3 or 4 days; or all 5 days. Or say you can't recall.

screens.why1: After two questions about whether I got my call list booked, asking which part of my week I'd most want made easier makes sense, and it puts the calling next to everything else that pulls me away from it.
screens.why2: Prior auths, rooming, vitals, check-in and refill requests are all words I use every day, so I can answer on the first read.
screens.why3: Every one of these is something I did myself last week, especially covering the front desk when we were short.
screens.why4: The options fit my job, but 'answering the phones and refill requests' is two jobs in one, and charting or the inbox messages, which eat my time too, is missing.
screens.why5: Calling patients due for a screening is just one choice among my real chores, and nothing tells me about any product or uses words I wouldn't say.
screens.why6: It is one short question with five short options I can hold in my head, and the 'none of these' at the end is easy to say back.
screens.instead: Think of your last week at the clinic. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Getting prior authorizations through; covering check-in at the front desk; rooming patients and taking vitals on time; reaching patients due for a screening; or keeping up with refill requests and messages. Or say none of these.

screens.why1: Asking how my last stretch of outreach calls went fits after the booking questions, but the first option, every patient called and booked, just repeats what screens 1 and 2 already asked me.
screens.why2: "Your last outreach call" sounds like one phone call, while the options are about the whole list, and "calling, texting" asks about two different things in one breath, so I'd have to stop and work out what it means.
screens.why3: Working the due list between rooming patients is exactly what I do, so I can answer from my own day.
screens.why4: "Most called," "got through part of it" and "called a handful" run into each other, the first option mixes calling with booking, and "nobody called the list" doesn't fit a question that starts from my last call.
screens.why5: "Calling, texting" reads like someone's notes pasted in rather than how I'd say it, and texting appears in the stem but not in any of the options.
screens.why6: "How did calling, texting patients due for a visit go" stumbles when heard because the comma doesn't come across, though the five short options are easy to hold.
screens.instead: Think of the last day you worked the call list. How far did you get through it? Called everyone on it; called most, a few left over; got through about half; called only a few; didn't get to it that day. Or say you can't recall.
